## The course in one paragraph

Vibe coding, building software by describing intent to an AI and iterating on what it produces, has collapsed the cost of a working prototype from weeks of engineering to hours of a manager's time. This elective puts that capability in the hands of MBA students with no programming background. Over five 4-hour workshops, teams take one real problem from their own organizations to a deployed web application with an integrated language-model capability, evaluate the security, privacy, cost and maintainability risks of what they built, decide between build, buy and hand-off, and present a working product and business case to a panel on Demo Day.

## Who it is for

MBA students and managers who need to test ideas, specify what they need from technology teams, and judge AI-built software, without becoming programmers. No coding experience is required or assumed.

## What students leave with

- A deployed, working AI-powered application built for a problem they chose.
- A tested test set and a risk memo for that application.
- A build / buy / vibe decision framework they have applied once.
- A first-hand understanding of what has changed in the economics of building software, and of what remains a defensible advantage.

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Credits | 2 SCT-Chile (20 contact hours + 25 autonomous = 45 hours) |
| Format | 5 workshop sessions of 4 hours, teams of 2 to 3 |
| Language | English (deliverables in English or Spanish) |
| Assessment | 5 weighted components, no final exam, pass at 55/100 |
| Competencies | CE1, CE2, CE4 (CE3 secondary); CGT1, CGT2, CGT3 |
